description: one coherent real scenario: 3 decision types (choice/score/noul) over ONE state batch and ONE backbone forward on Yelp/yelp_review_full

dataset.label_semantics: class index y in 0..4 == (y+1) stars; Q1 choice label = y, Q2 score label = y (levels 0..4), Q3 noul label = 1[y == 0]

splits.test_source: official test split, first 1500 rows (cap applied=True)
splits.train_cal_source: disjoint stratified carve from the official train split (bc.make_splits)

questions.choice: What star rating will this reviewer give?
questions.score: On a 0-to-4 scale, how many stars does this review earn?

protocol.joint: one loader interleaves all three decision types inside every epoch, so state_proj / E_Q / E_C / fusion are updated by all three losses; each type's head sees only its own loss
protocol.shared_features: the same precomputed [N, 128] matrices for all three questions

3_calibration.fit_split: calibration split ONLY (never train, never test)
3_calibration.note: JevXForDecision holds ONE calibration engine per model, so a mixed decide() call applies a single calibrator to all three types. The scenario therefore fits one engine PER QUESTION TYPE and reports the per-type temperatures; the live decide() call in phase 4 runs the raw (uncalibrated) model.

4_live_decide_invariants.call: JevXForDecision.decide(input_ids=<tokenized test batch, truncation=True, max_length=128>, questions=3, decision_type=['choice','score','noul'], options=[K=5, levels 0..4, None])
4_live_decide_invariants.why_pre_tokenized: the live path never truncates a state and raises above the backbone's learned position table; the same tokenizer call bc.featurize() makes (max_length=128) is used so the live call and the featurize-once training features see identical tokens

featurized_vs_live.note: identical modules; the residual is float re-association between two independently batched runs of the same arithmetic, plus the padding-width difference between the two batches

matched_padding_walk.scheme: every solo call padded to max_length so both calls share one tensor width

checks.note: the batched call pads to the longest state in the batch, a 1-row call pads to that row's own length, so the two passes reduce the same arithmetic over different tensor shapes; the comparison is a numerical bound, not a bitwise identity

6_quality_test.split: test (first 1500 rows of the official test split)

baselines.b1_linear_probe: single Linear(128 -> 5) on the identical frozen features, same splits/seeds/hyperparams

7_risk_coverage.question: Q1 choice (K=5)
7_risk_coverage.confidence: max probability AFTER temperature scaling fit on the cal split

selective_prediction.rule: thresholds = quantiles of the CAL-split confidence; the test split is only scored at those thresholds

7_risk_coverage.note: AURC is the mean of the empirical risk over the n coverage points 1/n..1 (bench_common.aurc).

8_printed_decisions.source: live JevXForDecision.decide() over the test batch (phase 4 output), plus the same call with confidence_threshold=0.9
8_printed_decisions.probabilities_shown: raw (uncalibrated) model probabilities; the per-type temperatures are reported in phase 3 / phase 6
8_printed_decisions.selection_rule: 3 highest-confidence correct + 3 highest-confidence wrong + 2 rows at the median confidence + the 2 lowest-confidence rows, all taken from the live decide() output; at threshold 0.9 1496/1500 Q1 rows abstained, so the abstained flag is reported per row rather than used to select rows

protocol.label_derivation: dataset ClassLabel y in 0..4 (== y+1 stars); Q1 label = y, Q2 level = y, Q3 label = 1[y == 0]. All three questions are scored against REAL dataset labels on the same state.
